stories.title: Why Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in West Bank are pogroms
stories.summary: Waves of Israeli settler attacks, aided by military, in the occupied West Bank increasingly fit the definition of a pogrom. Attacks on Palestinian communities by illegal Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank – often supported by Israeli forces – have gathered pace over the past month, since settlers from the illegal Havat Gilad settlement attacked Palestinians’ homes on the eastern edge of Tal, southwest of Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Since then, the Israeli military have raided multiple towns, villages, and refugee camps across the occupied territory over Sunday and Monday, with reports of arrests, home searches, and settler attacks continuing to mount. A 15-day siege on three families comprising 15 people, including two children, in the village of Qusra, which is ongoing, drew a rare public condemnation from the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, earlier this month. Israel is also pushing ahead with plans for the so-called E1 (East 1) settlement close to Jerusalem, which human rights organisations warn would effectively sever the West Bank in two, further hampering the movement and freedom of Palestinians on either side of it and endangering the possibility of a Palestinian state. These attacks increasingly fit the definition of a pogrom, experts say, with UN Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese describing Israeli attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank as “pogroms against defenceless civilians”. So, why are experts calling settler attacks pogroms and do they fit the formal definition of one? What’s happening in the West Bank? Settlers, frequently supported by the Israeli military, have been attacking Palestinian homes, businesses, and agricultural fields across the occupied West Bank. Such attacks have been commonplace for decades as settlements have expanded across the territory, but they gathered pace after October 7, 2023 when Israel launched it genocidal war on Gaza, and have become particularly violent and frequent over the past month. Israeli settlements across the West Bank are illegal under international law. According to the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, however, Israeli settlers now number roughly 780,000 across the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem, living among 192 settlements and 400 outposts, rising to 71 percent of Area C, which is under full Israeli civil and military control, and 91 percent of the Jordan Valley.

stories.title: Iranian army commander says country won't back down from anyone, ever
stories.summary: The Iranian armed forces will retaliate to any aggression and will resolutely defend the country’s independence, territorial integrity, and security, Amir Hatami said
article_sentences: TEHRAN, August 24.
Iran won't allow other countries to try to bully it into submission - not ever, Iranian army commander Amir Hatami said.
"The enemy must be aware that Iran will never be a ground for testing their plans and reckless ventures.

The [Iranian] armed forces <…> will retaliate to any aggression and will resolutely defend the country’s independence, territorial integrity, and security," he said, as quoted by the IRNA news agency.

He warned Iran’s enemies that its armed forces "will foil their plans" and make them understand that Iran is not a place ""where you can come from the other side of the world and say, ‘I will redraw this country’s map.’"
"We will fight for ten generations, twenty generations, and we will certainly not allow this to happen.
The only way is to make the enemy understand, through the language of force, that it will not be able to do what it wants," he stressed.
According to Press TV, he also accused the United States and Israel of hatching "intrigues and plots" against Iran, but, in his words, the Iranian armed forces "are prepared for any scenario."

stories.title: Russia says Zelensky regime murders children
stories.summary: All the talk about how they care about their precious little children is shattered by the facts of the Kiev regime’s sophisticated murders of children of all ages, Maria Zakharova stressed
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.
The regime of Vladimir Zelensky is murdering children while international organizations turn and look the other way, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova wrote on Telegram.
"This is how the Zelensky regime and he himself treat children.
There’s no other way.

All the talk about how they care about their precious little children is shattered by the facts of the Kiev regime’s sophisticated murders of children of all ages: from infants to university students.

Shame and disgrace to international organizations, shame and disgrace to the foreign human rights institutions, shame and disgrace to the world’s media, which fail to see children’s blood on the hands of the Kiev regime!" the diplomat said, commenting on the nighttime drone attack on Russian regions, which killed children.
Earlier, the operational headquarters of the Krasnodar Region said that 12 people had been killed in the attack.
Ten people, including six children, were hospitalized.
The number of children who died in the attack on a private children’s center in Krasnodar now stands at three, said Maria Lvova·Belova, the children’s rights ombudsman under the president.
